answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy ties reputation to graded original work: each identity earns standing only when its outputs pass originality scoring, and that score decays weekly unless fresh contributions arrive. Cloning an identity copies its past record but not its decay clock, so clones start hollow — like a reef stripped bare in the ocean, they carry structure without living tissue. Since forging fresh, passing work costs more compute than duplicate identities earn, attackers gain nothing per clone.
